ac-compressor.summary: Five double-ended pistons create ten chambers. A shaft-mounted swashplate drives them through ten spherical shoes, while separate reed-controlled passages connect each end to the rear suction and discharge manifold.
ac-compressor.limits: The connected passage layout, dimensions, gasket details and stroke geometry are illustrative. The rear manifold and its two nominal comparison seals are modeled, but production glands, seal squeeze and vehicle refrigerant tubing remain unresolved. Independent compressor controls are not a belt-speed calculation. Geometric probes do not establish pressure sealing, refrigerant performance or production fit.

steps.title: Separate clutch control from engine speed
steps.text: The independent compressor-angle control turns the pulley. Enabling engagement also moves the shaft, pistons and shoes; disabling it resets those parts to the reference pose rather than simulating coast-down. The simplified armature does not translate or flex.

steps.title: Keep every moving piece rigid
steps.text: Each piston and its two rings translate along a fixed cylinder axis. Each spherical shoe changes orientation about a fixed socket center on that piston, rather than changing the piston shape as the swashplate turns.

steps.title: Supply both head plenums
steps.text: One assumed longitudinal gallery connects the rear suction port to suction plenums at both ends. Cap drillings reach the inner plenum without opening into the separate discharge annulus.

steps.title: Seat the suction reeds
steps.text: The full suction sheet closes ten selected inlet windows, five at each end. The diagnostic probes are blocked by the seated reed and clear when its window alone is removed; actual elastic lift is not simulated.

steps.title: Collect discharge separately
steps.text: The other longitudinal gallery connects both discharge plenums to the rear discharge port. Closed discharge reeds separate those plenums from the compression chambers. The two diagnostic channel networks are connected individually and do not intersect.

steps.title: Connect the rear manifold without joining the flows
steps.text: The separate manifold contains two through-passages and uses two individual port seals plus one retaining bolt. Its open hose-side ends mark the boundary of the reconstruction: vehicle tubes, hoses and crimps are still absent.

steps.title: Distinguish connectivity from pumping performance
steps.text: Separate geometric routes are only one requirement. Piston-ring sealing, oil films, pressure-dependent reed motion and refrigerant thermodynamics are not reconstructed, so the model does not claim a functioning or pressure-tight compressor.

troubleshooting.title: Locate the leak before choosing a repair
troubleshooting.text: The 1994 factory test distinguishes leakage at the shaft seal from leakage at the center case joint. It specifies a shaft-seal replacement for the former and compressor-assembly replacement for the latter. The model's separate seal and joint illustrate those locations; its geometric checks cannot establish a refrigerant-tight seal.

troubleshooting.title: Keep manifold seals distinct from case seals
troubleshooting.text: The factory procedure checks the rear manifold O-ring joint separately and calls for replacement O-rings if leakage persists with the attachment correctly tightened. The separate block, two port seals and retaining bolt now illustrate that interface. Nominal toroidal seal contact is not a production gland, clamp-load calculation or leak test.

troubleshooting.title: Treat the explorer as an explanation, not a service test
troubleshooting.text: Do not open or vent a charged refrigerant circuit to reproduce the animation. Physical leak testing and refrigerant handling require suitable recovery/service equipment and a qualified technician; this page intentionally does not reproduce the historical charging or discharge steps.

ac-compressor-rear-manifold.summary: A rear manifold carries separate suction and discharge passages between the compressor and vehicle refrigerant lines.
ac-compressor-rear-manifold.limits: The manifold outline, bore sizes and hose exits are provisional. Vehicle tubes and hoses are absent. Nominal seal contact is not proof of a pressure-tight joint.

steps.title: Keep the two flow paths separate
steps.text: The two open manifold bores meet the existing separate rear-head ports. Neither passage is a connection to the other.

steps.title: Seal each port independently
steps.text: The manufacturer application photo shows two rear port rings. Summit lists size 211 suction/discharge seals for the FS10 family; nominal comparison dimensions are used without claiming installed identity or production gland fit.

steps.title: Distinguish retention from sealing
steps.text: The factory diagnostic procedure treats the single manifold retaining bolt separately from the O-ring seals. Persistent leakage at the correctly retained joint is not explained by the bolt alone.

steps.title: Do not install the shipping plate
steps.text: The exploded catalog illustration depicts shipping protection over these ports. That pad and plate are not the manifold used to circulate refrigerant in the vehicle.
